source_text:
Homilia habita in ecclesia Cyrini
Τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἐξ ὁμιλίας ῥηθείσης ἐν τῇ Κυρίνου ἐκκλησίᾳ,
τρισκαιδεκάτῃ τοῦ φαμενὼθ μηνὸς κατ' Αἰγυπτίους, ἐν ᾗ τὸ τοῦ Ἠσαΐου
ῥητὸν ἑρμηνεύει τὸ φάσκον· Κατέπιεν ὁ θάνατος ἰσχύσας καὶ πάλιν
ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου.
Ὁ μὲν γὰρ τῶν ὅλων θεός, ἅτε δὴ ζωὴ καὶ ζωοποιὸς ὑπάρχων, ἄφθαρτον ἐπὶ
γῆς ζῷον ἠθέλησεν εἶναι τὸν ἄνθρωπον, εἰ <καὶ> φύσεώς ἐστι φθαρτῆς. Ὁ δέ,
ἐπείπερ ἦν πονηρὸς καὶ βάσκανος, ἐπεβούλευσε τῷ γένει, ἀντετάττετο τῇ βουλήσει
τοῦ δημιουργοῦ, κατεκόμισε πανούργως εἰς παρακοήν, εἰδὼς ὅτι πεσεῖται δι' αὐτῆς
εἰς θάνατον.
thought_title: God's will for humanity and the adversary's plot
orientation: Cyril is opening his homily by stating the lemma from Isaiah and then beginning his narrative about God's intention for humanity and the adversary's opposition.
pass_a_gloss: Homily delivered in the church of Cyrinus. Of the same, from a homily delivered in the church of Cyrinus, on the thirteenth of the month Phamenoth according to the Egyptians, in which he interprets the saying of Isaiah that says: Death swallowed having prevailed, and again God removed every tear from every face. For the God of all things, since indeed he is life and life-giving, willed that the human being be an incorruptible living creature on earth, even if he is of corruptible nature. But he, since indeed he was wicked and envious, plotted against the race, was opposing the will of the Creator, brought it down cunningly into disobedience, knowing that through it it will fall into death.

choices.english: an incorruptible living creature on earth
choices.why: Keeps the adjective-noun order and the literal sense of ζῷον as living creature, preserving the paradox of incorruptibility on earth.
rejected: an imperishable living being on earth

choices.english: even if he is of corruptible nature
choices.why: Renders the concessive force of εἰ καὶ and the genitive of quality literally, keeping the tension between God's will and human nature.
rejected: even though he has a corruptible nature

choices.english: was opposing the will of the Creator
choices.why: The imperfect tense shows ongoing opposition, and 'Creator' renders δημιουργοῦ as a distinct title for God in this context.
rejected: opposed the will of the Creator
was setting himself against the Creator's will

choices.english: brought it down cunningly into disobedience
choices.why: κατακομίζω has a downward motion sense that fits the fall narrative; 'cunningly' captures the adverbial force of πανούργως.

choices.term: εἰδὼς ὅτι πεσεῖται δι' αὐτῆς εἰς θάνατον
choices.english: knowing that through it it will fall into death
choices.why: The future tense πεσεῖται is kept as future, and δι' αὐτῆς is rendered literally as 'through it' to preserve the causal link to disobedience.
rejected: knowing that through it he would fall into death
knowing that by it he would fall into death

bible_refs.note: Κατέπιεν ὁ θάνατος ἰσχύσας καὶ πάλιν ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου

pass_b_english: The God of all things, since he is life and life-giving, willed that humanity be an incorruptible living creature on earth, even though its nature is corruptible. But the adversary, because he was wicked and envious, plotted against the human race. He was opposing the will of the Creator. He cunningly brought humanity down into disobedience, knowing that through it humanity would fall into death.

last_rejected.quote: He was opposing the will of the Creator.
last_rejected.why: Source has one compound sentence with three verbs; English splits into separate sentence, losing that adversary did all three things as one continuous action.
last_rejected.fix: plotted against the human race, opposed the Creator's will, and cunningly brought humanity down into disobedience
last_rejected.ruling: Splitting one Greek sentence into two English sentences is stylistic; no meaning is lost or changed.
